analysis:
This PR is documentation-only. docs/reference/configuration.md gets a date bump and a new "Add-on hold" section (patch lines 149-164). docs/reference/protocol-messages.md gets a date bump and a new "Add-on hold busy fields" section (busy_reason, busy_since_ms, busy_addon) plus small edits at other ranges. I examined the supplied head text for configuration.md (lines 308-752), which is unchanged surrounding content, and the patch excerpts for the changed ranges. The protocol-messages.md unit had only metadata and a truncated patch, so the changed ranges at head 284, 383 and 1445 were not visible. No code, control or default changed in the visible evidence.

Security-relevant claims in the new docs, which should be checked against the source:
- The add-on socket is local, at ~/.darkbloom/runtime/addon.sock. DARKBLOOM_ADDON_SOCKET is tests-only and is not in the LaunchAgent passthrough list. DARKBLOOM_ADDON_DEV_IDENTITY is DEBUG-only and adds one extra TEAMID:identifier. AddonPeerPolicy.current is stated to gate peers by code-signing identity. The release build is supposed to ignore both variables, so a local-process spoofing check (TB-003, T-044-style) should confirm AddonPeerPolicy enforces code-signing peer verification and that release builds never read the dev identity variable. The source was not supplied.
- The hold reports heartbeat.status=draining with busy_addon, a code-signing identifier or 'operator'. This is provider-reported, adversarial-provider data, so the coordinator must treat it as untrusted and must not let it affect authorization. It does not grant serving permission, and the hold never sends provider_drain. The hold returns on the same connection, so T-053 (stale authorization across connection changes) is unaffected as documented. The register message carrying busy fields is a new wire surface. Whether unknown busy_reason values are handled safely is stated as mapping to absent.
- Availability: a local add-on can hold the Mac and take it out of serving for up to 600 s per lease. This is a local DoS or availability lever and depends on peer policy. A hold-ownership lock and addon-hold.json are documented, but their implementation was not reviewed.

No concrete regression is shown by docs alone. The next review pass should examine the Swift source (AddonHoldPaths, AddonPeerPolicy, ProviderBusy, CoordinatorClient+Registration) and the coordinator handling of the busy fields. These were not supplied.
